summary: This work investigates circuit-level fault tolerance for logical Pauli-rotation (Trotter) circuits implemented on the [[8,3,3]] non-CSS stabilizer code using block-level constructions that preserve the Trotter pattern under encoding. A circuit-level memory pseudo-threshold of $1.5\times10^{-3}$ is established for the Chao–Reichardt protocol, but the encoded Trotter implementation exhibits asymmetric logical-$X$ and logical-$Z$ failure channels due to phase faults on the parity ancilla propagating into undetectable logical operators with trivial syndrome.
motivation: Small high-rate non-CSS codes offer compact platforms for encoded quantum computation, but their mixed-Pauli stabilizers and limited native transversal gates complicate fault-tolerant implementation. Understanding whether block-level logical constructions can preserve fault tolerance when the algebraic Trotter mapping is applied to codes without rich gate sets is essential for near-term quantum simulation.
method: Single-fault analysis of the [[8,3,3]] code's encoded Pauli-rotation circuit identifies the circuit-distance-one mechanism: a $Z$ fault after the phase gate propagates through the parity-uncomputation CNOT ladder to produce $Z_2^{\overline{}}$, an undetectable logical operator. Flag-conditioned recovery, CliNR resource verification, flag postselection, and biased-noise models are evaluated, and a diagnostic protected limit with ideal phase gates and flag couplings is constructed to identify required protection levels.
result: No tested mitigation achieves simultaneous suppression of both logical sectors under realistic noise. CliNR and flag postselection strongly suppress one sector while leaving the orthogonal axis (aligned with the rotation) above unencoded reference rates. The diagnostic limit with Z-biased Trotter noise and idealized phase/flag CNOTs restores pseudo-threshold behavior in both sectors, approaching memory-benchmark performance and revealing that suppressing identified first-order Trotter faults leaves Chao–Reichardt recovery as the dominant contribution.
